title: The Nakai misl
hookLine: a misl of the Nakka country south-west of Lahore

cards: Run back over the names so far. Bhangi: a nickname. Ahluwalia, Kanhaiya, Sukerchakia: villages.
Ramgarhia: a fort. Most of those names are a small map of where a band came from. Today's band went wider.

Its name points at neither one man nor one village, but at a whole stretch of country south-west of Lahore that people called the Nakka. The riders were the people of that land. Today: the Nakai misl.

teach.h: THE NAKKA COUNTRY, BETWEEN THE RIVERS.
teach.b: Three things. First, the land. Tradition places the Nakka country south-west of Lahore, in the stretch between the rivers.
It was farming country. The Nakai riders came from its villages and held them. They weren't strangers who rode in and took a district.
They were its own people, organized as a band of the Khalsa. Second, the founder.
Tradition says the band grew around a Sikh named Hira Singh, who took amrit, joined the Khalsa, and gathered riders from his country.
In the way Sikh histories tell it, the Nakai band wasn't among the largest, and didn't make the loudest noise in the Dal Khalsa. It held its own corner. Third, where the Nakai name turns up later.

teach.h: A NAKAI DAUGHTER MARRIES RANJIT SINGH.
teach.b: A daughter of the Nakai family married the young Ranjit Singh, whose band you met yesterday. Tradition says she became the mother of his heir.
So the quiet band of the Nakka country was woven into the family that ruled from Lahore. Bands from different corners of the Punjab were being tied together, by marriage as much as by riding.
Under all of it, a misl's name kept its origin in plain sight. Say Nakai, and people in the Punjab would know which fields and villages you meant.

teach.h: A BAND THAT CARRIED ITS HOME IN ITS NAME.
teach.b: The band carried its home in its name.

how: Sikhs meet the Nakai misl in Sikh histories as the band of the Nakka country, and the Nakai name is remembered through the marriage that tied it to Maharaja Ranjit Singh's family.

practice: Say silently the name of a place that matters to you: your hometown, your street, the neighborhood your family came from. Do you know what it means, or who it was named for?
If not, just wonder; if so, let the meaning sit with you, and if you pray, breathe Waheguru as you hold the place in mind.

wordCard.voice: Nakka, the stretch of country south-west of Lahore that gave the Nakai misl its name, gathered by Hira Singh, later tied by marriage to the house of Ranjit Singh. Today's word.

carryVoice: Your line: named for the land. A name can carry a home inside it. That's day eight hundred ninety-three.
